about: Seed structural compatibility rules for scripts/check_stack.py. Tags, not products. A rule fires when every layer named in 'when' provides all listed tags ('brief' means brief.tags). 'requires' then demands the named layer provide all listed tags; 'excludes' forbids any of them. Project-local rules go in the stack block with cited evidence.

rules.why: Files written to an ephemeral filesystem are lost on restart or redeploy.
Several instances cannot safely share one embedded single-writer database file.
Short-lived function instances exhaust connection-per-client databases unless a pooler or HTTP access sits between them.
Server push (WebSockets, SSE, streams) needs connections held open longer than a request.
Server rendering needs a running server; static hosting serves files only.
Offline operation needs a client that works without the network and a protocol to reconcile changes later.
Edits made offline on several devices conflict; the authoritative store needs a defined policy.
Money movement needs atomic multi-record writes and retries that cannot double-apply.
Accounts need an authentication decision; it is not implied by any other layer.
Regulated personal data carries audit and protection obligations across layers.
Accepting writes in several regions needs replication and a defined conflict policy.
Browsers block cross-origin calls unless the API is same-origin or sends CORS headers.
